classification.difficultyReason: Locate the elevation angle in differently oriented diagrams, then choose either a right-triangle complement or equal alternate angles to determine its size.

content.prompt: Mark the angle of elevation $\theta$ and find its size.

spec.description: Horizontal base, vertical right side and rising line of sight. Dashed horizontal extends left from the upper vertex. Right-angle marker at the lower-right vertex.
spec.mathematics: The given 70° lies at the upper-right vertex between the line of sight and downward vertical. The requested elevation angle is at the lower-left vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: The given 70° is visible; the supplied blue θ = 20° annotation is excluded.

answer.short: $\theta=20^{\circ}$, marked at the bottom-left vertex between the horizontal base and the line of sight.
answer.worked:
Mark $\theta$ at the bottom-left vertex, between the horizontal base and the line of sight.

$\begin{aligned}\theta+70^{\circ}+90^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\\theta+160^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\\theta&=20^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Angles in a triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Vertical left side, horizontal base and descending line of sight. Dashed horizontal extends right from the upper-left vertex. Right-angle marker at the lower-left vertex.

answer.short: $\theta=30^{\circ}$, marked at the bottom-right vertex between the leftward horizontal base and the line of sight.
answer.worked:
Mark $\theta$ at the bottom-right vertex, between the leftward horizontal base and the line of sight.

$\theta=30^{\circ}$ because alternate angles on parallel horizontal lines are equal.
